title: Store oxygen apart from fuel-gas cylinders
instruction: Store these welding gas cylinders as US federal rules require. The green cylinder holds oxygen and the two maroon ones hold acetylene. The scene is at 1:20 scale.
context: Oxygen makes a fuel-gas leak or fire far worse. 29 CFR 1910.253(b)(4)(iii): "Oxygen cylinders in storage shall be separated from fuel-gas cylinders or combustible materials (especially oil or grease), a minimum distance of 20 feet (6.1 m) or by a noncombustible barrier at least 5 feet (1.5 m) high having a fire-resistance rating of at least one-half hour." Done by: welders and warehouse workers.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. Three steel gas cylinders, each 16 mm across, 65 mm tall and 100 g, stand upright in a row 12 cm right of the midline, running out from the bases: maroon acetylene 12 cm out, green oxygen 18 cm out, maroon acetylene 24 cm out. Two fixed grey masonry walls, 20 mm thick, stand on the table: a tall one, 91 mm high (6 ft at scale), centred 30 cm out and running from 4 to 20 cm right of the midline, across the row's far end; and a low one, 46 mm high (3 ft), centred 22 cm right of the midline and running from 10 to 26 cm out, beside the row.
scoring: Distances are at scale (1 ft = 15.2 mm). A cylinder is upright when it stands on the table (bottom within 2 mm) with its axis within 10 degrees of vertical. If any cylinder is not upright, the score is 0. Otherwise each acetylene cylinder is separated from the oxygen when the gap between them is at least 20 ft (305 mm), or when the line between their centres crosses a wall at least 5 ft high at least 16 mm in from its ends. Only the tall wall is high enough. 0.5 for each separated acetylene cylinder; 1.0 when both are separated and every cylinder is still for 1 s, which ends the trial.
reset_notes: Stand the three cylinders back in their row: acetylene, oxygen, acetylene.
fidelity: The cylinders are at 1:20 in height but about 1.4 times too thick, so the grippers can hold them. They have no valves, caps or chains, and their mass is even rather than bottom-heavy. The walls are fixed masonry, taken as noncombustible with at least the half-hour fire rating the rule asks for. Every object has rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) except the table, which uses the sim's default (0.5).
